Note::TexAccessor::inline_math¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::inline_math() const

Extract Inline Formulae Without Mixing In Displays¶

inline_math() extracts complete inline-math regions from every Text cell. It recognizes both authored forms, $...$ and \(...\), and retains the opening and closing delimiters in each token. Keeping the delimiters makes the result suitable for source inspection or relocation without guessing which spelling the author chose.

The method deliberately excludes $$...$$ and \[...\] display regions. Use display_math for only those regions, or math_blocks when inline and display forms belong in one source-ordered stream. A single-dollar region may not cross a physical newline; an escaped dollar does not close it. Parenthesized inline math may span lines and is closed by the next unescaped \).

Scanning is lexical rather than a TeX execution step. Delimiters inside a comment or macro argument still have their ordinary byte-level meaning, and the method neither expands commands nor evaluates formulae. An escaped opener, an unmatched opener, and plain text contribute no token. Empty but balanced regions are valid and are returned with their delimiters.

The result is a TokenBatch: tokens() is a flat Text Note in cell and source order, while offsets() is an Int64 Note with one boundary per receiver cell plus the final boundary. Cell i owns [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]). This representation preserves ownership for a matrix or higher-rank receiver without padding cells to a common token count. Undefined input produces undefined tokens and offsets [0]; every defined non-Text dtype is rejected.

The scanner visits each source byte once and copies only matched regions. It does not build a syntax tree. The token Note owns its strings, so it remains valid after the receiver is destroyed.

Example 1: Separate Inline And Display Forms¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        R"(price \$5; $x+\$y$ then $$display$$ and \(z\))",
        "\\[block\\] and $line\nbreak$", R"(\(unfinished)", "plain"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto result = source.tex().inline_math();

std::cout << result.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["$x+\\$y$", "\\(z\\)"]

The escaped dollar inside the first formula is content, not its closer. Both display regions are excluded, the newline prevents $line...break$ from forming one inline region, and the unmatched \( is ignored.

Example 2: Recover Matrix-Cell Ownership¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = result.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 2, 2, 2]

Both tokens came from the first logical cell. The remaining three matrix lanes own empty half-open ranges.

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().inline_math();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().inline_math();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "inline math Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false offsets=[0]
inline math Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • display_math: extract only display-math regions.

  • math_blocks: merge all four math-region forms in source order.

  • add_math_delimiters: make each complete cell one math region.
